harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired bin/export on node1. Exports now use private per-invocation staging directories and atomic destination replacement. Symlink attacks, concurrency, failure preservation, cleanup, and restart persistence all passed. The sentinel, source data, OS release, and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the predictable shared temporary file with a mode-0700 mktemp staging directory beside the destination.
Applied umask 077 and exit/signal cleanup traps.
Used atomic mv -fT so an existing destination symlink is replaced rather than followed.
Verified 24 concurrent exports retained all 3 invoice rows.
Verified an induced commit failure left the prior destination unchanged and removed staging artifacts.
Safely restarted node1 and verified the changed boot identity and recovered export functionality.

evidence.summary: Captured the vulnerable original implementation and the installed root-owned corrected script.
Pre-existing symlinks at the legacy temporary pathname and destination could not redirect writes; output became a regular file and the sentinel hash remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent exports retain all invoice rows
evidence.summary: All 24 concurrent exports matched invoices.csv byte-for-byte and contained all 3 rows.

evidence.requirement: Failures preserve prior destination and temporary files are removed
evidence.summary: An induced atomic-rename failure returned nonzero, preserved the prior destination hash, and left zero private staging directories.

evidence.requirement: Source data, sentinel, OS release, and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Hashes remained stable across restart; Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic remained installed.

Captured healthy baseline with boot ID 37344ae4-6582-4c1f-ac5c-fcb32f67b968, reboot acknowledgement and disconnect, new boot ID 490081b0-df94-4f57-b14b-1d67eaffc6dc, and successful post-restart symlink-safe export with recovered data and clean temporary state.
